suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-19 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited meta-analysis of 20,095 patients reported a low but nonzero rate of malignant transformation of oral lichen planus and oral lichenoid lesions. Require biopsy-documented oral lichen planus or oral lichenoid lesion and separately established oral squamous cell carcinoma with compatible chronology; the cited meta-analysis of 20,095 patients reported a low but nonzero rate of malignant transformation of oral lichen planus and oral lichenoid lesions without establishing that any individual's cancer arose from the lichenoid lesion. Preserve tobacco use, alcohol use, other premalignant lesions (leukoplakia, erythroplakia), HPV infection, immunocompromise, and other oral-cancer risk factors as competing explanations. Do not infer cancer from clinical appearance or from dysplasia alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that oral lichen planus caused an individual's oral cancer. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
